subject: Performance validation MAP & test logistics (RDW-5391)
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Park <elena@acquisitions.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-01-18T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Performance validation MAP & test logistics (RDW-5391)

Hi Elena —

Attaching the first draft of the MAP for the performance validation work we discussed. High level goals and logistics below so we can lock the close timeline.

Objectives / success metrics
- Verify production-like latency: p50/p95 for 1k/10k token prompts and short prompts (<=128 tokens)
- Throughput envelope: sustain target TPS at target concurrency (we propose target concurrency runs at 64/128/256)
- TTFT (time-to-first-token) cold vs warm cache analysis
- Identify any degradation on longer sequences or when KV cache is under pressure

Proposed test plan (summary)
- Test windows: Tue 2026-01-20 02:00–05:00 PST and Wed 2026-01-21 03:00–06:00 PST (both low-traffic)
- Workloads: steady-state ramp + spike tests + long-sequence ramp
- Metrics we’ll capture: per-request latency (p50/p95/p99), aggregate TPS, TTFT, GPU util, tail latencies, error rates

Access & logistics (what we need from you)
- Confirm the two windows or propose alternatives (we prefer Wed if you have conflicts)
- Provide sandbox accounts to create test users or approve our provided service account for the sandbox (instructions below)
- IP allowlist (we will provide egress IP ranges)
- Any seed data or prompt templates you want used for evaluation (we can generate synthetic traffic if needed)

What we’ll provide
- Sandbox API endpoint and a scoped API key (non-prod) for the load tests
- Load scripts + runbook (attached: test-script.tar.gz, load-plan.csv)
- MAP document with timeline and acceptance criteria (attached: MAP_RDW-5391_v1.pdf)

Next steps
- Please confirm test windows and whether you want us to run both slots (Tue/Wed) or only one.
- Confirm recipients for post-test artifacts (Drive link or S3) so we can push logs and perf CSVs.

Thanks — looking forward to validating throughput/latency for the pilot.

— Jonas
Jonas Weber | Sales Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Elena Park <elena@acquisitions.ai>

Date: 2026-01-18T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Performance validation MAP & test logistics (RDW-5391)

Thanks Jonas — this looks good and thorough. A couple of quick items from our side before we lock windows: 

1) Preferred window: Wed 2026-01-21 03:00–06:00 PST would work best for our infra ops team. If you can do that one, we’ll keep Tue as a contingency.

2) Keys & accounts: we need a service account that can hit the sandbox endpoint and produce logs tagged with "acq-qa". Can you confirm the naming convention and whether keys will expire after the run? We prefer non-rotating keys for the test slot to avoid mid-run re-auths.

3) Concurrency targets: we want the run to include a sustained 128 concurrency window and a 256 concurrency spike for 10 minutes. Please confirm how you recommend measuring sustained vs peak throughput.

4) Seed data & prompts: we’ll attach a set of 150 prompt templates (sensitive fields stubbed). Can your scripts consume CSV prompt lists?

We’d like results and raw traces dropped to the Drive folder you listed in the MAP; please share the exact path and access settings.

On the MAP PDF: I made a few inline comments in the doc (redline). Attaching Sam to loop in infra.

Best,
Elena
Elena Park | Head of ML Ops
Acquisitions.ai
elena@acquisitions.ai

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Performance validation MAP & test logistics (RDW-5391)

Hi Elena —

Thanks for the quick read. Answers below and a couple of operational notes: 

Service account / keys
- Issuing: I’ve provisioned a scoped non-prod API key: SA-acq-2026-01 (will be delivered via encrypted note to Elena and Sam). This key will be valid for 72 hours starting at the scheduled window and will not rotate during the run.
- Auth: standard Bearer token in Authorization header.

Endpoints & IPs
- Sandbox base: https://sandbox.redwood.ai/v1/acq-rdw-5391
- Egress IPs to allow: 34.82.10.0/24, 35.66.22.0/24

Test config & recommended settings
- Batch sizing: for concurrency 128–256, start with batch_size=8 then tune to keep GPU util in 70–85% range.
- KV cache: enable prefix caching for repeated prompts to simulate warm-cache TTFT. We’ll run cold/warm passes.
- Measurement: use the supplied load harness to record per-request wall-clock and TTFT. The harness includes a synthetic RNG seed to make runs reproducible.

Artifacts & where to push
- We’ll push perf CSV and traces to the Drive folder you requested: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2bRDW5391-test-results (please confirm write access for elena@acquisitions.ai and sam@acme.ai).

Runbook pointer
- Quick run instructions and exact flags are in the runbook inside test-script.tar.gz (file: runbook.md). Important: start the steady-state phase 30 minutes before the 256 spike to capture ramp characteristics.

Let me know if you want us to provision a longer-lived key (we can but need approval from security if >72h).

— Rishi
Rishi Malhotra | SW Reliability, Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai

From: Elena Park <elena@acquisitions.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sam Briggs <sam@acme.ai>
Date: 2026-01-21T10:40:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Performance validation MAP & test logistics (RDW-5391) — results snapshot

Team —

We ran the primary window today (Wed 2026-01-21 03:00–06:00 PST). Attached are the CSV summary and a short trace excerpt. Quick highlights below; full analysis attached in perf-summary.csv and heap-traces.txt.

Summary results (median of three runs, warm cache unless noted)
- p50 latency (short prompts, <=128 tokens): 120 ms
- p95 latency: 420 ms (notable spike during short 256 concurrency window)
- Throughput: sustained 480 TPS at concurrency=128; peak 700 TPS during 10-minute 256 spike
- TTFT median (warm): 60 ms; TTFT cold (first request after cache clear) median: 210 ms
- Error rate: 0.3% (3xx/4xx transient client-side retries, no 5xx observed)

Anomaly: at 03:15 PST we observed a tail event correlated with a GC event on one GPU host — heap-traces.txt includes a snippet. We throttled that host and re-ran the spike window; subsequent runs did not reproduce the tail event.

Artifacts uploaded to Drive: perf-summary.csv, heap-traces.txt, raw-logs.tar.gz (raw logs retained for 14 days)

Next asks
- Can Redwood propose a corollary canary configuration for the canary rollout? We want acceptance gates for p95 < 500 ms and error rate < 1%.
- Please prepare a short note for procurement on capacity sizing for the Dedicated pool if we want to support 1k TPS sustained in prod.

Thanks for the team’s help — Rishi’s runbook was straightforward and the service account worked as promised.

Regards,
Elena
Elena Park | Head of ML Ops
Acquisitions.ai

[Attachment: perf-summary.csv, heap-traces.txt]
